study type: Randomized controlled trial with longitudinal and cross-sectional analyses
exposure: Timing of prophylactic antibiotics during cesarean section (before skin incision vs. after umbilical cord clamping)
outcome: Infant gut microbiome (bacterial composition, metabolic pathways, short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, bacterial strain level, load of antibiotic resistance genes)
cohort: The study participants included women delivering via a scheduled cesarean section who received prophylactic antibiotics either before skin incision or after umbilical cord clamping, and their infants (28 infants for longitudinal analysis, 79 infants from 3 cohorts for cross-sectional analysis).
finding: Antibiotic administration during cesarean section has only limited effects on the early-life infant gut microbiome, with subtle differences observed at the bacterial strain level and in the load of antibiotic resistance genes, while feeding mode was a predominant factor.
mod_finding: Antibiotic administration during cesarean section has only limited effects on the early-life infant gut microbiome.
